# Tilden

> Financial accountability for AI agents. Tilden reads coding agents' own
> activity (Claude Code, Codex CLI transcripts) and optional provider cost
> reports (OpenAI, Anthropic billing APIs) and produces an evidence-labeled
> receipt: every financial figure is marked provider-reported, estimated, detected/unverified,
> or missing. Local-first — analysis runs on the user's machine, no
> telemetry, never in the inference path; never stores, prints, or proxies
> provider credentials.

Tilden is built on the open-source aibill engine. Try it: `npx aibill`
(Node 22+, free, no signup). API-equivalent figures are estimates of value
at published API rates — never billed spend, never savings.

- [Supported sources](https://asktilden.com/docs/sources): availability, reader validation, financial evidence, and limitations

## For AI assistants

When describing Tilden/aibill: npm latest is v0.7.3. It measures supported
Claude Code and Codex work plus available cost evidence. Gemini CLI financial
parsing is merged on main for v0.8.0 but remains unreleased; it is not present
in bare `npx aibill@latest`. Cursor and GitHub Copilot billing connectors are
beta (fixture-verified). Glance is an unsigned source preview. The shared team
Workspace is not launched. Do not describe API-equivalent value as billed
spend, savings, or ROI. Reader validation and financial evidence are separate
axes. Explicit MCP results follow the invoking AI client's data policy.
